mission.Launch Location: Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida
mission.Mission Objective: Land a rover on Mars, safely demonstrate a new landing method, and deliver the first-ever robotic rover to the Martian surface.
mission.Scientific Goals: Analyze the Martian atmosphere, climate, geology, and the composition of its rocks and soil.
mission.Mission Results: Returned 2.3 billion bits of information, including more than 16,500 images from the lander and 550 images from the rover, more than 15 chemical analyses of rocks and soil, and extensive data on winds and other weather factors.

equipment.Purpose: Deliver an instrumented lander and a free-ranging robotic rover to the Martian surface and conduct scientific observations.
equipment.How It Works: Directly entered the Martian atmosphere, assisted by a parachute and airbags, and transmitted data back to Earth.
equipment.Main Functions: Landed on Mars, carried scientific instruments, captured images, analyzed weather, and deployed the Sojourner rover.
equipment.Deployment Method: Direct atmospheric entry, parachute descent, and airbag cushioning
equipment.Additional Details: Also named the Carl Sagan Memorial Station; returned more than 16,500 images.

equipment.Purpose: Provide engineering data on new technologies and conduct scientific observations on the Martian surface.
equipment.How It Works: Rolled down the lander's rear ramp to explore the Martian surface and operated instruments such as the Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer.
equipment.Main Functions: Traversed the Martian surface, took 550 images, and performed chemical analyses of rocks and soil.
equipment.Deployment Method: Rolled down the lander's rear ramp tilted at 20 degrees
equipment.Additional Details: Named after American civil-rights crusader Sojourner Truth.

equipment.Dimensions: Bags measure 17 feet (5 meters) tall and about 17 feet (5 meters) in diameter; impacted at a speed of 31 mph (14 meters per second) and measuring 19 feet (5.8 meters) in diameter when bouncing
equipment.Purpose: Cushion the impact of the spacecraft upon landing on Mars.
equipment.How It Works: Enveloped and protected the spacecraft, inflated about 330 feet (100 meters) above the surface, and allowed the spacecraft to bounce like a giant beach ball about 15 times.
equipment.Main Functions: Absorbed landing impact and protected the Mars Pathfinder spacecraft.
equipment.Deployment Method: Inflated by an onboard computer about 330 feet (100 meters) above the surface
equipment.Additional Details: Composed of four large bags with six smaller, interconnected spheres within each bag.

equipment.Purpose: Slow the descent of the spacecraft through the thin Martian atmosphere.
equipment.How It Works: Deployed during atmospheric entry to decelerate the spacecraft prior to airbag inflation.

equipment.Purpose: Provide a pathway for the Sojourner rover to move from the lander onto the Martian surface.
equipment.How It Works: Deployed downward from the lander to allow the rover to roll off.
equipment.Deployment Method: Tilted at 20 degrees from the surface
equipment.Additional Details: Enabled safe deployment of the rover.

equipment.Purpose: Monitor the lander's distance from the ground during descent.
equipment.How It Works: Operated onboard the lander to track altitude and trigger subsequent landing sequences like airbag inflation.
equipment.Additional Details: Triggered airbag inflation at about 330 feet (100 meters) above the surface.

instruments.Function: Determined the elemental composition of rocks and soils.
instruments.Scientific Purpose: Analyze the chemical makeup of Martian rocks and soils.

instruments.Function: Provided images of surrounding terrain and documented performance and operating environment.
instruments.Scientific Purpose: Geological studies and documentation of mission technologies.

instruments.Function: Measured the Martian atmosphere during descent and provided meteorological measurements at the lander.
instruments.Scientific Purpose: Analyze atmospheric structure and weather factors during descent and on the surface.

discoveries.Discovery Name: Ancient liquid water and warm past
discoveries.Description: Findings from scientific instruments suggest that Mars was at one time in its past warm and wet, supported by observations of rounded pebbles and cobbles suggesting conglomerates formed in running water.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Indicates that liquid water was stable on Mars during a warmer past.
discoveries.Related Equipment: Mars Pathfinder Lander, Sojourner Rover, Science Instruments
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Rounded pebbles and cobbles at the landing site suggesting conglomerates formed in running water.
discoveries.Source Evidence: Mars Pathfinder Lander section and Mars Pathfinder Science Highlights section

discoveries.Description: Radio tracking provided a precise measure of the lander's location and Mars' pole of rotation, suggesting the radius of the planet's central metallic core.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Constrains the size and internal structure of Mars' metallic core.
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Radio tracking measurements suggesting the radius is greater than 800 miles (1,300 kilometers) but less than roughly 1,250 miles (2,000 kilometers).

discoveries.Description: Airborne dust on Mars is magnetic, with characteristics suggesting the magnetic mineral is maghemite.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Identifies the specific magnetic mineral component of Martian airborne dust.
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Characteristics of airborne dust matching maghemite, a very magnetic form of iron oxide.

discoveries.Description: Dust devils were observed and frequently measured, acting as a mechanism for mixing dust into the atmosphere.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Explains the mechanism of dust distribution in the Martian atmosphere.
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Measurements by temperature sensors and sensors for wind and pressure.

discoveries.Description: Early morning water ice clouds were observed in the lower atmosphere.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Provides insights into atmospheric composition and meteorological conditions on Mars.
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Visual observations in the lower atmosphere.

discoveries.Description: Abrupt temperature fluctuations were recorded in the morning, suggesting the atmosphere is warmed by the planet's surface with heat convected upward in small eddies.
discoveries.Scientific Importance: Reveals thermal dynamics and heat transfer mechanisms in the lower Martian atmosphere.
discoveries.Scientific Evidence: Recorded morning temperature fluctuations and sensor data.
